content: 1. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF (tenofovir disoproxil fumarate) is indicated as a complete regimen for the treatment of HIV infection in treatment-naïve adults. It is also used as a replacement for a current antiretroviral regimen in patients who are virologically suppressed (HIV-1 RNA <50 copies/mL) on a stable antiretroviral therapy (ART) regimen for at least 6 months, with no history of treatment failure and no known substitutions associated with resistance to the individual components of Stribild. The recommended dose is one tablet taken orally once daily with food. 2. For pediatric patients aged 12 years or older and weighing at least 35 kg, elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF is indicated as a complete regimen for treatment-naïve individuals or as a replacement for a stable ART regimen in virologically suppressed patients (HIV-1 RNA <50 copies/mL) for at least 6 months, with no history of treatment failure or resistance to the components of Stribild. Safety and efficacy have not been established in children under 12 years of age. The recommended dose is one tablet taken orally once daily with food. 3. There is no data available to make dose recommendations for pediatric patients with renal impairment. 4. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF is a complete regimen for HIV and should not be co-administered with other antiretroviral agents. 5. Cobicistat, a CYP3A4 inhibitor, increases the levels of drugs metabolized by CYP3A4, such as alfuzosin, dihydroergotamine, ergotamine, methylergonovine, pimozide, lovastatin, lurasidone, and midazolam (oral). Co-administration with these drugs is contraindicated due to the risk of serious or life-threatening events associated with elevated plasma concentrations. 6. Drugs that induce CYP3A4, such as carbamazepine, dexamethasone, fosphenytoin, phenobarbital, phenytoin, rifabutin, rifampin, and oxcarbazepine, decrease the levels of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF. This may lead to a loss of virologic response and the development of resistance. Co-administration with these drugs is contraindicated. 7. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases the levels of drugs such as lomitapide, lonafarnib, mavacamten, naloxegol, and pacritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with these drugs is contraindicated due to the risk of severe adverse effects, including systemic toxicity and opioid withdrawal symptoms (in the case of naloxegol). 8. Co-administration of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF with flibanserin is contraindicated due to the risk of severe hypotension or syncope. Flibanserin should not be used with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 9. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, such as cobicistat, increase the systemic exposure of drugs like mavacamten, which may result in heart failure due to systolic dysfunction. Co-administration is contraindicated. 10. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF should not be co-administered with other antiretroviral agents, such as atazanavir, darunavir, efavirenz, enfuvirtide, fosamprenavir, indinavir, lamivudine, lopinavir, maraviroc, nelfinavir, nevirapine, raltegravir, or etravirine, as it is a complete regimen for HIV treatment. 11. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases the levels of drugs like regorafenib and isavuconazonium sulfate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of altered drug exposure and potential toxicity. 12. For parenteral midazolam, dose reduction should be considered when co-administered with elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF, as cobicistat increases midazolam levels. However, oral midazolam is contraindicated. 13. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases the levels of drugs like geprione and ivabradine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of severe adverse effects. 14. Cobicistat significantly increases lomitapide levels, and co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of severe toxicity. 15. Co-administration of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF with naloxegol is contraindicated, as it can significantly increase naloxegol systemic exposure, potentially leading to opioid withdrawal symptoms. 16. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, such as cobicistat, increase the levels of drugs like regorafenib, which may decrease the exposure of its active metabolites (M-2 and M-5). Co-administration is contraindicated. 17. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases the levels of drugs like finerenone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 18. Drugs like primidone decrease the levels of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This may lead to a loss of virologic response and resistance. Co-administration is contraindicated.
